filings.business_description: UiPath derives substantially all of its revenue from its UiPath Platform, an automation platform used by customers. It earns revenue from software licenses, maintenance and support, hosted SaaS access, and professional services; license revenue is recognized when the license is transferred, while SaaS and maintenance and support revenue are recognized over time. The filing describes investments intended to expand customer adoption and sales, develop platform capabilities including AI, and grow distribution channels. (10-K Item 1A)
filings.risk_factors_summary: The company warns that it has incurred net losses and may not sustain profitability, including because of significant operating expenses and non-cancellable cloud-capacity commitments. It identifies macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions, trade-policy changes, tariffs, and reduced customer spending as potential pressures on demand and operations. The company also faces risks from competition, technology change including AI and ML, customer renewal and expansion, and the possibility that its platform may not meet customer needs. (10-K Item 1A)
filings.mda_highlights: Not available in provided sources. Item 7 is not available; the provided text only states in Item 1A that fiscal 2026 revenue was $1,610.6 million, up from $1,429.7 million in fiscal 2025, and that ARR was $1,852.6 million at January 31, 2026, up from $1,666.1 million at January 31, 2025. (10-K Item 1A)
filings.geographic_revenue_breakdown: Sales outside the U.S. accounted for 54% of fiscal 2026 revenue. A China-specific split and a fuller U.S./other geographic revenue breakdown are not available in provided sources. (10-K Item 1A)
filings.governance_red_flags: The filing refers to securities class action suits as a possible category of lawsuits, but does not identify a specific pending or threatened securities class action, claim period, or allegations. This is a risk disclosure, not a disclosed specific lawsuit. (10-K Item 1A)

citations.claim: Revenue sources and recognition model (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: We derive our revenue from the sale of our software licenses for use of our proprietary software, maintenance and support for our licenses, right to access certain products that are hosted by us (i.e., SaaS), and professional services.

citations.claim: The company derives substantially all revenue from its platform (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: We derive and expect to continue to derive substantially all of our revenue from our UiPath Platform™.

citations.claim: Growth and competitive strategy includes platform development, customer expansion, international penetration, and channel development (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: These initiatives include increasing our overall customer base and expanding sales within our current customer base, continuing to penetrate international markets, investing in research and development to improve the capabilities of our platform (including AI capabilities), acquiring businesses, technology, talent, and related integration efforts, growing our distribution channels and channel partner ecosystem, deepening our user community, hiring additional employees and investing in our existing workforce, expanding our operations and infrastructures both domestically and internationally, and incurring expenses related to legal, accounting, and other administrative expenses aspects of operating as a public company.

citations.claim: The company identifies profitability and cloud capacity commitments as risks (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: We have entered into non-cancellable multi-year capacity commitments with certain third-party cloud providers for cloud infrastructure services.

citations.claim: The company identifies macroeconomic, geopolitical, trade-policy, and tariff risks (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: Trade policies and disputes have resulted and may in the future result in increased tariffs, trade barriers, and other protectionist measures, which can make our products less competitive, reduce demand for our products, limit our ability to sell to certain customers, or impede or slow the movement of our products across borders.

citations.claim: The filing states that sales outside the U.S. accounted for 54% of fiscal 2026 revenue (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: Moreover, sales outside the U.S. accounted for 54% of our revenue for fiscal year 2026.

citations.claim: The filing mentions securities class action suits in a general risk disclosure, without identifying a particular pending case (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: If our quarterly or annual results of operations fall below the expectations of securities analysts or investors who follow our stock, the price of our Class A common stock could decline substantially, and we have faced and could in the future face lawsuits that are costly and may divert management’s attention, including securities class action suits and derivative actions.

citations.claim: Fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025 revenue and ARR figures stated in the available text (10-K Item 1A).
citations.excerpt: We generated revenue of $1,610.6 million and $1,429.7 million for fiscal years 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a growth rate of 13%. Our ARR was $1,852.6 million and $1,666.1 million at January 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a growth rate of 11%.
